title: Fixed-ring valued sheaves and modules over the constant ring on a sieve site
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$: its covering sieves contain the maximal sieve and satisfy pullback of sieves and transitivity. A sieve is a collection of arrows into a fixed object closed under precomposition. A presheaf with values in sets, abelian groups, rings or modules is a sheaf when every covering-sieve matching diagram is a limit diagram. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ are assumed. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $\Lambda^{\mathrm{pre}}$ be the constant ring presheaf with identity restriction maps, and let $\underline\Lambda=(\Lambda^{\mathrm{pre}})^\#$ be its ring sheafification, with unit $\iota:\Lambda^{\mathrm{pre}}\to\underline\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

Let $\operatorname{Sh}_J(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda})$ be the category of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules which are sheaves, with $\Lambda$-linear natural transformations. Let $\operatorname{Mod}_J(\underline\Lambda)$ have as objects abelian sheaves $N$ equipped, at each $C$, with an $\underline\Lambda(C)$-module structure on $N(C)$, compatible with restrictions by $(s x)|_{C'}=s|_{C'}x|_{C'}$; its morphisms are natural transformations linear over $\underline\Lambda(C)$ at each $C$. This is the category of sheaves of $\underline\Lambda$-modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Restriction of scalars along $\iota$ gives an additive equivalence
$$\operatorname{Mod}_J(\underline\Lambda)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}_J(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda}).$$
For every fixed-$\Lambda$ module-valued sheaf $N$ there is a unique $\underline\Lambda$ action on its same underlying abelian sheaf extending its original action along $\iota$. Every natural transformation linear for the original fixed-$\Lambda$ actions is linear for these extended actions. This action extension is a quasi-inverse equivalence retaining the underlying abelian sheaves and their maps. There is no nonzero-ring or nonempty-site hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, is the scalar-extension prototype; this agent-extracted constant-ring equivalence is stated on arbitrary Grothendieck covering-sieve topologies, as required by former step 2 of the dense comparison. Its no-fibre-product scope is supported by the generic GrothendieckTopology constructions in Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Presheaf/Sheafification.lean:54-72,125-150; no claim that the ordinary pretopology statement supplies that scope without this extension.

proof.text: Identify the fixed-$\Lambda$ presheaves with presheaves of modules over $\Lambda^{\mathrm{pre}}$: the identity ring restrictions make semilinearity precisely $\Lambda$-linearity. A covering-sieve matching family is a compatible tuple of sections; these tuples form a $\Lambda$-module by componentwise operations. Its projections give the matching limit both in modules and in abelian groups. The comparison from sections is linear, and a bijective linear map has a linear inverse. Hence a fixed-module presheaf is a module-valued sheaf exactly when its underlying abelian presheaf is a sheaf. This also shows that restriction along $\iota$ lands in the category claimed in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent constant-ring specialization on covering-sieve topologies using lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification (Mathlib Sheafification.lean:54-172).

proof.text: Use the module-sheafification construction of [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification] with the constant ring presheaf and with the identity map from the underlying abelian presheaf of N to the same abelian sheaf N. The identity is locally bijective, so Mathlib PresheafOfModules.sheafify supplies a module sheaf whose abelian sheaf and section maps are definitionally those of N. This specializes the same sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] without constructing a separate inverse to the usual sheafification unit.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent constant-ring specialization on covering-sieve topologies using lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification (Mathlib Sheafification.lean:54-172).

proof.text: The action is the real construction PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.module with the identity abelian unit, not a witness chosen from an existence theorem. The constructor supplies its module laws and semilinear restrictions. The map PresheafOfModules.toSheafify is fixed-ring linear and its underlying map is the identity, so its linearity gives iota(a) acting as the original scalar a. This defines E(N) on exactly the original sections.

proof.text: Given two extended actions m,n on N, bundle them as module sheaves. A fixed-ring linear natural map between their scalar restrictions is formed using their extension equations. Mathlib PresheafOfModules.restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective lifts it to a map linear over the sheafified ring, with unchanged components. Apply this to the identity of N. Its linearity identifies the two scalar multiplications, and Module.ext' identifies the module structures sectionwise.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent constant-ring specialization on covering-sieve topologies using lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification (Mathlib Sheafification.lean:54-172).

proof.text: For any fixed-ring linear natural transformation f:N to M and any extended actions on N and M, form the restricted module-presheaf morphism using the extension equations. The same restriction Hom equivalence lifts f to a map linear over the sheafified ring, whose section maps remain f. Apply this in particular to the constructed actions to define E(f); identities, composition and addition hold componentwise.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent constant-ring specialization on covering-sieve topologies using lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification (Mathlib Sheafification.lean:54-172).

proof.text: Restriction $R$ along $\iota$ retains abelian sheaves and their maps, and step 3 gives $RE(N)=N$ with the original fixed-ring action; the same holds on maps. For any $\underline\Lambda$-module sheaf $Q$, its own action and the action of $E(RQ)$ both extend that of $RQ$, so step 4 identifies them. Thus $ER(Q)=Q$, again with identity underlying maps, yielding natural identity isomorphisms for both composites. Finally addition of morphisms in both categories is componentwise addition of abelian homomorphisms. Both $R$ and $E$ retain those maps, hence preserve zero and addition. These functors give the stated additive equivalence.
